subject.title: Feature: Subscribe to WhatsApp call events (Baileys)

question: Should OpenClaw add opt-in inbound WhatsApp Baileys call-event tracking, and which sanitized surface should expose that activity to agents?
rationale: The missing listener is clear, but call metadata affects privacy, access control, retention, and user-visible contact/activity semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent exposure model.

options.title: Approve opt-in plugin-owned tracking
options.body: Add a default-off WhatsApp plugin listener for Baileys call events, sanitize and filter metadata like inbound messages, and expose contact activity through one documented surface.

options.title: Design the extension surface first
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers decide whether this belongs in plugin hooks, session metadata, a contact-activity store, or a message tool query.

options.title: Decline inbound call tracking
options.body: Close the direction if OpenClaw should avoid storing or exposing WhatsApp call metadata even when Baileys emits it.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in plugin-owned tracking
recommendation.body: Add a default-off WhatsApp plugin listener for Baileys call events, sanitize and filter metadata like inbound messages, and expose contact activity through one documented surface.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest WhatsApp plugin history and authored the adjacent outbound-call implementation and prior scoping comments.
